The video is a slideshow of static screenshots and document images, cycling through several distinct "scenes":

1. (Frames 1–3, repeated) A screenshot of a FactPost (@factpostnews) tweet stating "Every House Rules Republican votes to block the Epstein Files Transparency Act from advancing," accompanied by a photo of a white-haired woman seated at a committee table with a nameplate reading "MS. FOXX." Below the tweet screenshot is a white caption box reading "at what point did Republicans decide hiding Trump's Epstein ties is more important than the dignity of the country?"

2. (Frame 4) A screenshot of a tweet from Karoline Leavitt (@PressSec) stating: "The latest piece published by the Wall Street Journal PROVES this entire 'Birthday Card' story is false. As I have said all along, it's very clear President Trump did not draw this picture, and he did not sign it. President Trump's legal team will continue to aggressively pursue litigation."

3. (Frames 5–6, repeated) A scan of a birthday card interior. The card's background features an outline drawing of a female torso/body silhouette. Inside is a printed script-style dialogue labeled "Voice Over," "Donald," and "Jeffrey," ending with "A pal is a wonderful thing. Happy Birthday—and may every day be another wonderful secret." The card bears the printed name "Donald J. Trump" and what appears to be a handwritten signature beneath it.

4. (Frames 7–8, repeated) A comparison graphic showing three signatures side by side: (top) labeled "EPSTEIN CARD" — a "Donald J. Trump" printed name with signature below; (middle) labeled "1995 LETTER TO LILLIAN VOLK" — a "Sincerely," with a similar "Donald" signature; (bottom) labeled "1999 LETTER TO LARRY KING" — a "Sincerely, Love Donald" with a similar signature. A prominent red banner overlaid reads "he wrote that card."
